words.tip: das Oktoberfest means Oktoberfest festival. die Oktoberfeste means Oktoberfest celebrations. For several separate celebrations, add -e. All German nouns start with a capital letter.

die Oktoberfeste
Singular: das Oktoberfest. Plural: die Oktoberfeste. For several separate celebrations, add -e. The famous Munich event is normally named in the singular.

das
For one, say das Oktoberfest; for more than one, say die Oktoberfeste.

nounForms.rule: For several separate celebrations, add -e. The famous Munich event is normally named in the singular.

memory.scene: Picture an October festival with music and a giant pretzel. Oktober + Fest joins October and festival.
memory.watch: Write Oktober with k, not the English c. Join Oktober and fest into one word; capital O.

words.translation: The harvest thanksgiving festival is in autumn.
words.tip: das Erntedankfest means harvest thanksgiving festival. die Erntedankfeste means harvest thanksgiving festivals. Add -e for several festivals. Build Ernte + dank + fest without spaces. Keep the e in Ernte and the k in dank. Learn the whole noun with its article. All German nouns start with a capital letter.
usages: The harvest thanksgiving festival is in autumn.
We celebrate the harvest thanksgiving festival.
forms: Write the plural of das Erntedankfest, including die.
die Erntedankfeste
Singular: das Erntedankfest. Plural: die Erntedankfeste. Add -e for several festivals.

das
For one, say das Erntedankfest; for more than one, say die Erntedankfeste.

memory.scene: Picture a harvest table: crops, a thank-you sign, and a festival. Ernte is harvest, Dank is thanks, and Fest is festival. It is not the American Thanksgiving holiday.
memory.watch: Build Ernte + dank + fest without spaces. Keep the e in Ernte and the k in dank.
memory.recall: Picture the scene, cover the German, and write das Erntedankfest. Check every letter and the article.

words.tip: die Wanderung means hike. die Wanderungen means hikes. Add -en: Wanderung → Wanderungen. Write Wander + ung: only one r in Wander. The noun ending -ung is a useful clue for die. Learn the whole noun with its article. All German nouns start with a capital letter.
forms: Write the plural of die Wanderung, including die.
die Wanderungen
Singular: die Wanderung. Plural: die Wanderungen. Add -en: Wanderung → Wanderungen.
Complete the singular: ___ Wanderung.
die
For one, say die Wanderung; for more than one, say die Wanderungen.

memory.scene: Picture a long hike along a forest trail. Connect Wanderung with English wander, but remember: this word names the hike.
memory.watch: Write Wander + ung: only one r in Wander. The noun ending -ung is a useful clue for die.
memory.recall: Picture the scene, cover the German, and write die Wanderung. Check every letter and the article.

words.tip: der Baum means tree. die Bäume means trees. Change a → ä and add -e. Singular Baum has au. Plural Bäume changes a to ä and adds e. Do not put the umlaut in the singular. Learn the whole noun with its article. All German nouns start with a capital letter.
forms: Write the plural of der Baum, including die.
die Bäume
Singular: der Baum. Plural: die Bäume. Change a → ä and add -e.
Complete the singular: ___ Baum.
der
For one, say der Baum; for more than one, say die Bäume.

memory.scene: Picture one blocky tree; now add another tree and two dots over the a. One Baum becomes several Bäume.
memory.watch: Singular Baum has au. Plural Bäume changes a to ä and adds e. Do not put the umlaut in the singular.
memory.recall: Picture the scene, cover the German, and write der Baum. Check every letter and the article.

words.tip: das Blatt means leaf. die Blätter means leaves. Change a → ä and add -er. Blatt ends in double t. Blätter keeps tt, changes a to ä, and adds er. Learn the whole noun with its article. All German nouns start with a capital letter.
forms: Write the plural of das Blatt, including die.
die Blätter
Singular: das Blatt. Plural: die Blätter. Change a → ä and add -er.
Complete the singular: ___ Blatt.
das
For one, say das Blatt; for more than one, say die Blätter.

memory.scene: Picture a leaf falling beside a tree. Give its stem two little branches to remind you of the two t letters. The word can also mean a sheet of paper; this wave uses leaf.
memory.watch: Blatt ends in double t. Blätter keeps tt, changes a to ä, and adds er.
memory.recall: Picture the scene, cover the German, and write das Blatt. Check every letter and the article.

words.tip: das Bauernhaus means farmhouse. die Bauernhäuser means farmhouses. Only the house part changes: Haus → Häuser; keep Bauern unchanged. Keep the n in Bauern. Singular ends haus; plural ends häuser, with ä. Capital B, no space. Learn the whole noun with its article. All German nouns start with a capital letter.

forms: Write the plural of das Bauernhaus, including die.
die Bauernhäuser
Singular: das Bauernhaus. Plural: die Bauernhäuser. Only the house part changes: Haus → Häuser; keep Bauern unchanged.
Complete the singular: ___ Bauernhaus.
das
For one, say das Bauernhaus; for more than one, say die Bauernhäuser.

nounForms.rule: Only the house part changes: Haus → Häuser; keep Bauern unchanged.

memory.scene: Picture the farmer’s house beside a field. Bauern + Haus builds one farmhouse word. Haus looks a little like English house.
memory.watch: Keep the n in Bauern. Singular ends haus; plural ends häuser, with ä. Capital B, no space.
memory.recall: Picture the scene, cover the German, and write das Bauernhaus. Check every letter and the article.

words.tip: der Kürbis means pumpkin. die Kürbisse means pumpkins. Add -se to Kürbis: the resulting ending is -isse, with ss. Kürbis has ü, one s, and no final e. Kürbisse has double s and a final e. Learn the whole noun with its article. All German nouns start with a capital letter.
forms: Write the plural of der Kürbis, including die.
die Kürbisse
Singular: der Kürbis. Plural: die Kürbisse. Add -se to Kürbis: the resulting ending is -isse, with ss.

der
For one, say der Kürbis; for more than one, say die Kürbisse.

nounForms.rule: Add -se to Kürbis: the resulting ending is -isse, with ss.

memory.scene: Picture a pumpkin with two seeds above it: the two dots belong over ü. On the pumpkin’s label, check Kürbis before adding more pumpkins.
memory.watch: Kürbis has ü, one s, and no final e. Kürbisse has double s and a final e.
memory.recall: Picture the scene, cover the German, and write der Kürbis. Check every letter and the article.

words.tip: der Igel means hedgehog. die Igel means hedgehogs. The noun spelling does not change; change the article der → die. Start with capital I, then gel. forms: Write the plural of der Igel, including die.
die Igel
Singular: der Igel. Plural: die Igel. The noun spelling does not change; change the article der → die.
Complete the singular: ___ Igel.
der
For one, say der Igel; for more than one, say die Igel.

nounForms.rule: The noun spelling does not change; change the article der → die.

memory.scene: Picture one hedgehog, then a family of hedgehogs. Their name stays Igel; only der changes to die.
memory.watch: Start with capital I, then gel. The long first vowel is written with just I: do not add an e.
memory.recall: Picture the scene, cover the German, and write der Igel. Check every letter and the article.

words.tip: die Laterne means lantern. die Laternen means lanterns. Add -n to Laterne. Say and write La-ter-ne. Keep the e between t and r, and the final e. Laternen adds n. Learn the whole noun with its article. All German nouns start with a capital letter.
forms: Write the plural of die Laterne, including die.
die Laternen
Singular: die Laterne. Plural: die Laternen. Add -n to Laterne.

die
For one, say die Laterne; for more than one, say die Laternen.

memory.scene: Picture carrying a bright lantern on an autumn evening. English lantern and German Laterne share many letters; look carefully at the different ending.
memory.watch: Say and write La-ter-ne. Keep the e between t and r, and the final e. Laternen adds n.

words.tip: For this lesson, learn neblig: neb-lig. Nebelig is also a correct German spelling, but your assigned word is neblig. The last three letters are lig. Keep lowercase n. In these sentences the describing word comes after ist or sind; use neblig unchanged. The other sentence words are supplied: you only fill in the describing word.

words.tip: Only four letters: t-r-ü-b. Keep ü; no final e. Listen to the rounded ü sound. In these sentences the describing word comes after ist or sind; use trüb unchanged. The other sentence words are supplied: you only fill in the describing word.

memory.scene: Picture a gray, gloomy sky with no bright sunshine. Two little clouds above the word remind you of the two dots on ü. Trüb describes dull weather here, not a sad person.
memory.watch: Only four letters: t-r-ü-b. Keep ü; no final e. Listen to the rounded ü sound.

words.tip: Build maler + isch. The last four letters are isch; keep the three-letter sch together. In these sentences the describing word comes after ist or sind; use malerisch unchanged. The other sentence words are supplied: you only fill in the describing word.

memory.watch: Build maler + isch. The last four letters are isch; keep the three-letter sch together.

words.tip: Write reg-ner-isch. The beginning is regn, not regen. Finish with isch, including sch. In these sentences the describing word comes after ist or sind; use regnerisch unchanged. The other sentence words are supplied: you only fill in the describing word.

memory.scene: Picture rain over your village. Regen means rain. Compare Regen and regnerisch: rain becomes the describing word rainy.
memory.watch: Write reg-ner-isch. The beginning is regn, not regen. Finish with isch, including sch.
memory.recall: Picture the scene, hide the word, and write regnerisch from memory. Check it letter by letter.

words.tip: Write k-ü-h-l. Keep both the two dots over ü and the silent h after it. In these sentences the describing word comes after ist or sind; use kühl unchanged. The other sentence words are supplied: you only fill in the describing word.

memory.watch: Write k-ü-h-l. Keep both the two dots over ü and the silent h after it.

words.tip: Build wasser + dicht with no space. Wasser has double s; dicht ends cht. Lowercase w. In these sentences the describing word comes after ist or sind; use wasserdicht unchanged. The other sentence words are supplied: you only fill in the describing word.

memory.scene: Picture water rolling off your rain boots. Wasser is water; dicht can mean sealed. Together, wasserdicht means waterproof.
memory.watch: Build wasser + dicht with no space. Wasser has double s; dicht ends cht. Lowercase w.

words.tip: Write d-i-c-h-t. Keep cht together; there is no second i or final e. In these sentences the describing word comes after ist or sind; use dicht unchanged. The other sentence words are supplied: you only fill in the describing word.

memory.scene: Picture fog packed so closely that you cannot see the next tree. Dicht means dense here. It can also mean sealed, as in wasserdicht; the sentence tells you which meaning fits.
memory.watch: Write d-i-c-h-t. Keep cht together; there is no second i or final e.

der
For one, say der Spaziergang; for more than one, say die Spaziergänge.
